problem.paragraph: (T/F) If it is possible to go from state $$i$$ to state $$j$$ in $$n$$ steps, where $$n \geq 0$$ , then states $$i$$ and $$j$$ communicate with each other.
(T/F) An irreducible Markov chain must have a regular transition matrix.
(T/F) If a Markov chain is reducible, then it cannot have a regular transition matrix.
(T/F) If the $$(i,j)$$ - and $$(j,i)$$ -entries in $$P^{k}$$ are positive for some $$k$$ , then the states $$i$$ and $$j$$ communicate with each other.
(T/F) The entries in the steady-state vector are the mean return times for each state.
(T/F) If state $$i$$ communicates with state $$j$$ and state $$j$$ communicates with state $$k$$ , then state $$i$$ communicates with state $$k$$ .

Show that the communication relation is transitive. Hint: Show that the $$(i,k)$$ -entry of $$P^{n + m}$$ must be greater than or equal to the product of the $$(i,j)$$ -entry of $$P^{m}$$ and the $$(j,k)$$ -entry of $$P^{n}$$ .

First note that states $$1$$ and $$3$$ communicate with each other, as do states $$2$$ and $$4$$ . However, there is no way to proceed from either state $$1$$ or state $$3$$ to either state $$2$$ or state $$4$$ , so the communication classes are $$\left\{ 1 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ and $$\left\{ 2 \text{,} 4 \right\}$$ .
